# Question 1

## 1.1 Read data and convert first column to Date

The first column in the provided CSV is a row index, not calendar dates. If your original `JPM.csv` has real dates, this works unchanged.
1.1 Find the attached JPM.csv file. Use as.Date() function to change the
first column to Date object.

```{r}
jpm <- read.csv("FE515_hw2_JPM.csv") 

# adjust path if needed
jpm[, 1] <- as.Date(jpm[, 1])          
colnames(jpm)[1] <- "Date"
head(jpm)
```

## 1.2

1.2 Plot the adjusted close price against the date object (i.e. date object as
x-axis and close price as y-axis) in red line (require no points). Set the
title as JPM, the label for x-axis as Date and the label for y-axis as
Adjusted Close Price.
```{r}
plot(jpm$Date, jpm$JPM.Adjusted, type = "l", col = "red",
     main = "JPM", xlab = "Date", ylab = "Adjusted Close Price")
```

## 1.3 
1.3 Create a scatter plot of close price against open price (i.e. open prices as
x-axis, and close prices as y-axis). Set the x label as ”Open Price” and y
label as ”Close Price”.
```{r}
plot(jpm$JPM.Open, jpm$JPM.Close,
     xlab = "Open Price", ylab = "Close Price")
```

## 1.4 

1.4 Use cut() function to divide adjusted close price into 4 intervals. Generate
a barplot for the frequencies of these intervals.

```{r}
adj_int <- cut(jpm$JPM.Adjusted, breaks = 4)
barplot(table(adj_int), xlab = "Adjusted Close Interval", ylab = "Frequency")
```

## 1.5
1.5 Generate a boxplot of volume against the 4 intervals of adjusted close
prices.

```{r}
boxplot(jpm$JPM.Volume ~ adj_int,
        xlab = "Adjusted Close Interval", ylab = "Volume")
```

## 1.6
1.6 Use par() function to create a picture of 4 subplots. Gather the 4 figures
from 1.2- 1.5 into ONE single picture. Please arrange the 4 subplots
into a 2 by 2 frame, i.e. a frame consists of 2 columns and 2 rows. 

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(jpm$Date, jpm$JPM.Adjusted, type = "l", col = "red",
     main = "JPM", xlab = "Date", ylab = "Adjusted Close Price")
plot(jpm$JPM.Open, jpm$JPM.Close,
     xlab = "Open Price", ylab = "Close Price")
barplot(table(adj_int), xlab = "Adjusted Close Interval", ylab = "Frequency")
boxplot(jpm$JPM.Volume ~ adj_int,
        xlab = "Adjusted Close Interval", ylab = "Volume")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

# Question 2


Estimate the volume of the unit sphere (which is just $\frac{4\pi}{3}$) by simulation.
we draw N points from three dimensional uniform distribution. In a 3-D co
ordinate system, the position for the points inside the 1/8 unit sphere is given
by
$$
x^2 + y^2 + z^2 \leq 1, \quad x, y, z \geq 0.
$$

$$
\text{volume of } \frac{1}{8} \text{ unit sphere} = \frac{\text{number of inner points}}{\text{number of total points}} \times 1
$$

Then we have the volume of the unit sphere.

$$
\text{volume of unit sphere} = 8 \times \text{volume of } \frac{1}{8} \text{ unit sphere}
$$

We can use the frequency of inner points to estimate the volume of 1/8
sphere.

```{r}
set.seed(515)
N <- 1e6
x <- runif(N); y <- runif(N); z <- runif(N)
inner <- sum(x^2 + y^2 + z^2 <= 1)

vol_eighth <- inner / N * 1      # eq. (2)
vol_sphere <- 8 * vol_eighth     # eq. (3)

cat("Estimated volume:", vol_sphere, "\n")
cat("True volume     :", 4 * pi / 3, "\n")
```


# Question 3
3.1
Implement a Linear Congruential Generator (LCG)
$$
X_{n+1} = (a X_n + b) \bmod m
$$
which generates pseudo-random number from uniform distribution using
m = 244944,a = 1597,b = 51749. (Hint. See details in lecture 5 and
example codes.)

```{r}
seed <- 1   # seed in global environment

LCG <- function(n){
  m <- 244944
  a <- 1597
  b <- 51749
  x <- rep(NA, n)
  x[1] <- (a * seed + b) %% m
  for(i in 1:(n-1)){
    x[i + 1] <- (a * x[i] + b) %% m
  }
  seed <<- x[n]       
  return(x/m)          
}
```


## 3.2 Chi-square (df = 10) sample
3.2 Use the LCG in the previous problem, generate 10000 random numbers
from chi-square distribution with 10 degrees of freedom (i.e. df = 10),
and assign to a variable.
```{r}
U <- LCG(10000)
X <- qchisq(U, df = 10)

summary(X)
```


## 3.3 Histogram with 40 bins
 Visualize the resulting sample from 3.2 using a histogram with 40 bins

```{r}
hist(X, nclass = 40, main = "Chi-square (df = 10) via LCG", xlab = "X")
```
